To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a series of carbazole dendrimers with an iridium(i) complex core and investigated the light-harvest energy transfer mechanisms by various spectroscopic methods.
the energy transfer efficiency is above 97% and that the light-harvesters are excited within 10 ps.

the light-harvest efficiency of the Ir-complex core was enhanced by connecting a carbazole-based dendron, and that the energy transfer from the dendron to the Ir-complex was confirmed by time-resolved spectroscopic measurements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the light-harvesters of carbazole-dendrons with a heteroleptiridium(iii)-based blue phosphorescent core complex.
a series of carbazole-based dendrimers with an Ir-complex as the core.
the light-energy harvesting mechanisms of the carbazole-dendrimer with a blue-phophorescent iridium(iiii) complex core.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the light-energy harvesting in these dendrimers proceeds by the Forster energy transfer mechanism, and the energy transfer efficiency is close to 100%.
a Förster-type mechanism dominates the energy transfer from the Cz-dendrimer to the Ir-core.

the energy transfer from the peripheral Cz dendrons to the Ir-complex core in the dendrimers is very efficient and fast, with the rate constants being approximately 2.5 × 107 s-1 (G1), >5 × 107 (G2), 2 × 107 (Cz2-Ir), and >1 × 107 (Ir-Cz8) s-1, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dendrimeric light-harvesters with a heteroletic iridium(i) complex core show a high efficiency in the light-energy harvesting process, which is based on the efficient energy transfer from the peripheral Cz- dendrons to the Ir-core-complex.
a heteroleptic Ir(iii) complex can act as a light-energy harvesting centre for Cz-dendrimers.
the energy-transfer efficiency from the Cz-dendrimer to the Ir-complex is very high, and that the energy transfer is very fast.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SVD analysis is an effective method for the analysis of complex energy transfer systems.
we have shown the importance of SVD analysis for time-resolved TA measurements.
we were able to use a global analysis to distinguish between different energy transfer mechanisms, and to determine the energy transfer rates and quantum yields of the individual processes.
